flashcards.q: What is Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) and what does it let you do?
flashcards.a: A training method that applies the contrastive loss at multiple nested prefix lengths of the same vector simultaneously, so any prefix (e.g. first 256 of 3072 dims) is itself a usable, gracefully-degraded embedding -- lets you truncate dimensions at inference time without retraining.

flashcards.q: Can you compare cosine similarity scores between two different embedding models?
flashcards.a: No -- each model learns its own vector space during training with no guaranteed alignment between models, so scores from different models are not comparable even if both are unit-normalized.

flashcards.q: What are the rough 2026 MTEB scores for Cohere embed-v4, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, and BGE-M3?
flashcards.a: Cohere embed-v4 ~65.2, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large ~64.6, BGE-M3 ~63.0 -- a ~2 point spread that rarely decides production outcomes vs. dimension/latency/language coverage.

flashcards.q: What does BGE-M3 unify in one model?
flashcards.a: Dense, sparse (learned lexical), and multi-vector (ColBERT-style) retrieval in a single 568M-param open-weight model supporting 100+ languages and 8192-token context.

flashcards.q: What is the storage cost of 10M chunks at 1536 dims float32, and after truncating to 512 dims?
flashcards.a: 1536d: 10M * 1536 * 4 bytes = 61.4 GB raw. Truncating to 512d via Matryoshka: ~20.5 GB, roughly 3x smaller with small recall cost on MRL-trained models.

flashcards.q: Why does mean pooling generally outperform CLS-token pooling for retrieval?
flashcards.a: Mean pooling averages all non-padding token embeddings, aggregating signal across the whole sequence; raw CLS embeddings from models not fine-tuned for sentence-level tasks were never optimized to summarize the whole input.

flashcards.q: What happens if you skip or apply inconsistently the query:/passage: prefix on an instruction-tuned embedding model?
flashcards.a: Retrieval quality degrades silently -- the model learned different subspace rotations for each role during training, and inconsistent prefixes break the geometric relationship the contrastive training established.

flashcards.q: What does switching embedding models actually require operationally?
flashcards.a: A full reindex -- re-embed the entire corpus (vector spaces are incompatible across models), rebuild the ANN index, and shadow-evaluate against the old pipeline before cutover. Not a config change.

flashcards.q: What are 2026 embedding API prices for OpenAI and Cohere?
flashcards.a: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small: $0.02/1M tokens. text-embedding-3-large: $0.13/1M tokens, 3072 dims. Cohere embed-v4: $0.12/1M tokens, 128K context, Matryoshka dims 256-1536.

flashcards.q: Why can quantization (int8/binary) degrade recall more unpredictably than Matryoshka truncation?
flashcards.a: Matryoshka's degradation is trained-in and validated across nested lengths by the loss function; quantization is typically applied post-hoc to an already-trained space with no guarantee of even tolerance across dimensions or models.

flashcards.q: What determines an embedding model's quality ceiling for a specialized domain?
flashcards.a: The quality of hard-negative mining during contrastive training (lexically similar, semantically wrong passages) -- a smaller domain-fine-tuned model often beats a larger general-purpose one on that domain.
